items.title: Complete Fides's Conditor setup: echelon-current 1.3.0 (Ordo 1.5.0) through conditor upgrade --current, plus the fsharp-nuget-library scaffold (buildable project, foundations, build-and-test, release workflow); supersedes fides#2
items.description: Fides was adopted by Conditor (praxis, ordo, percepta, dokimos, visual-engineering, communication-engineering, tutela) but had no .NET project, so the Dokimos check failed on main and on fides#2. Move the Registry authority to echelon-current 1.3.0 (linux-x64, sha256 f917318c...) with conditor upgrade --current (Ordo 1.4.2 -> 1.5.0), then add the fsharp-nuget-library scaffold (EchelonFoundry.Fides, the future WASM client package): a buildable solution for Dokimos, .echelon/foundations.json with Ordo 1.5.0, echelon-foundations.yml, build-and-test.yml, and the nuget-library release workflow.

items.title: Consolidate Fides's SSO requirements, record the hosting and provider decisions, and capture the dependency-ordered backlog
items.description: There was no requirements document. Consolidate issue #1 (FIDES-P0), the user decisions of 2026-10-08 (cloud-agnostic exchange with a pure core and an AWS-first hosting adapter, Azure possible; GitHub as the only provider behind an extensible model; Helix keeps its own sign-in) and the consumer sign-in requirements (Chrona, Summa, Signal, Arca) into docs/requirements/FIDES-REQUIREMENTS.md with FID-* IDs. Record DF-FIDES-2026-0001/0002. Capture the minimal slices before Chrona's sign-in. Add a test that every requirement is named by an open work item.

items.title: Fides slice 1: re-anchor the charter and context on SSO, with a context gate test (FID-CTX-001..003, issue #1)
items.description: Minimal slice; blocking context defect (issue #1 FIDES-P0). Replace the boilerplate PROJECT-CHARTER.md with Fides's purpose: the common Echelon authentication/SSO identity boundary, GitHub first, not GitHub forever. Reconcile README.md and context/ARCHITECTURE.md, CURRENT-STATE.md, DECISIONS.md and the queue so they cannot disagree. Add a repository-context test that fails if the charter or product identity reverts to unrelated boilerplate. Requirements: docs/requirements/FIDES-REQUIREMENTS.md section 2.

items.title: Fides slice 2: trust-boundary model and the decision on what GitHub authentication proves (FID-TB-001..006, issue #1)
items.description: Minimal slice. Depends on WI-0003. Define users, trust boundaries (browser application, exchange service, provider, data repository), token and session ownership (the client secret exists only server-side), exact-match registered redirect URIs per application, the relationship between sign-in, GitHub repository permissions and each application's own capabilities, and logout/revocation states. Write the decision record required by issue #1 on what GitHub proves versus what Fides owns. Needs the answers to OQ-FIDES-001 (GitHub OAuth App or GitHub App) and OQ-FIDES-002 (stateless or session service).

items.title: Fides slice 3: executable acceptance tests before production code - invalid state/nonce, replay, wrong callback, revoked identity, expired session, repository access denial, provider outage (FID-TEST-001)
items.description: Minimal slice. Depends on WI-0004. Issue #1 requires these tests before production implementation. Write them against the pure core's types, failing first, with a fake provider. They become the definition of done for WI-0004's model and the exchange slice.

items.title: Fides slice 4: extensible provider model with GitHub as the only provider (FID-PRV-001..004, decision FID-D-002)
items.description: Minimal slice. Depends on WI-0004. User decision 2026-10-08: start small, GitHub only, because Arca needs a GitHub token; keep the model extensible. A provider interface (authorization URL, code exchange, identity resolution, revocation, declared capabilities) and a GitHub implementation with the narrowest grant that gives Arca repository read/write (OQ-FIDES-001). Identity comes from the provider (GET /user), never a typed username. A second provider must need no consumer changes beyond configuration.

items.title: Fides slice 5: pure F# code-for-token exchange core - authorization code with PKCE, single-use state, replay refusal (FID-EXC-001..005)
items.description: Minimal slice. Depends on WI-0005 and WI-0006. A cloud-agnostic pure core (decision FID-D-001): request, configuration and provider responses in; response or typed refusal out. Clock, randomness, secret retrieval and HTTP are explicit effect requests. Validate state, PKCE verifier, redirect URI and client registration before calling the provider. Refuse replays. A provider outage gives a typed failure and never a partial session. Codes, tokens, secrets and verifiers never reach logs, telemetry or errors. Runs every WI-0005 exchange acceptance scenario against the core with the GitHub simulator (FID-TEST-001). Aegis binding is WI-0014.

items.title: Fides slice 6: AWS hosting adapter - Lambda behind API Gateway, client secret from Secrets Manager/SSM, infrastructure as code per environment (FID-HOST-001..003, FID-HOST-005)
items.description: Minimal slice. Depends on WI-0007. User decision 2026-10-08: AWS most likely, Azure possible, so target AWS first with a thin adapter. Translate API Gateway HTTP API events to and from the core's types; the core references no cloud SDK. Read the client secret at runtime from Secrets Manager or SSM. Reproducible infrastructure as code, separate test/staging/production stacks and OAuth registrations, and CORS limited to registered origins. Needs OQ-FIDES-003 (account, region, domain).

items.title: Fides slice 7: WASM client library and Arca token provider - sign-in, callback, session states, retention modes (FID-CLI-001..004)
items.description: Minimal slice; the last one Chrona's sign-in needs. Depends on WI-0007. An F# client usable from Limen/Forma WASM applications: start sign-in, complete the callback, typed session states (signed out, signing in, signed in, expired, revoked, provider unavailable), and retention modes (memory-only default, session-scoped, persistent only by explicit choice with a clear action). Cross-tab signalling is an optimization only. It exposes a token provider matching Arca's token-provider port (ARCA-AUTH-001) without Arca referencing Fides. Runs every WI-0005 callback and session acceptance scenario against the client (FID-TEST-001). Published as a pinned package.

items.title: Fides: shared hosting-adapter conformance suite (FID-TEST-002, FID-HOST-004)
items.description: Depends on WI-0008. A suite every hosting adapter must pass with identical observable behaviour, so the Azure adapter can be added later without touching the core.

items.title: (Deferred) Fides Azure hosting adapter - Azure Functions plus Key Vault (FID-HOST-004)
items.description: Depends on WI-0010. Kept possible by decision FID-D-001; build only when Azure hosting is chosen.

items.title: Fides: release workflow and echelon-registry entry for the client package and exchange artifact
items.description: Depends on WI-0009. Release the client package (FID-CLI-004) and the core, hosting and AWS Lambda artifacts through the Echelon release contract as Sigstore-attested GitHub release assets (DF-FIDES-2026-0006; nuget.org dormant until NUGET_USER), register Fides in echelon-registry, and declare it so applications (Chrona first) pin it. Helix is not a consumer for now (decision FID-D-003).

items.title: Make the Dokimos quality check pass: regenerate the test project as a dotnet test (xUnit) project so the gate gets TRX test evidence
items.description: fides#3 run 37749426810: the build succeeded, but the Dokimos gate reported required-evidence-unavailable (exit 3). The policy (.dokimos/policy.json) requires tests.total and tests.failed, which come from the TRX that 'dotnet test --logger trx' writes, and the scaffold's console test runner is invisible to dotnet test. Root cause fixed in Conditor (conditor#54). Regenerate the scaffold test project and workflows with it, port the requirements traceability check to xUnit facts, and keep the gate enabled and unchanged.

items.title: Classify the exchange host's unexpected failures through Aegis (FID-EXC-005 Aegis clause)
items.description: Correction: EchelonFoundry.Aegis.Core 1.0.0 is on nuget.org (an earlier check queried the non-existent id echelonfoundry.aegis and wrongly recorded Aegis as unpublished). Bind the hosting runtime to it: capture unexpected failures at the host boundary as Aegis faults with stable FIDES.* codes and a 500 internal_error answer that discloses nothing, report provider outages and contract violations as Aegis faults, and deliver to standard error so the Lambda logs carry them.

items.title: Conditor's fsharp-nuget-library scaffold hides test output on failure: under bash -e, output=$(dotnet test ...) exits before echo
items.description: Found on fides#9: build-and-test and release.yml Test steps printed nothing when tests failed. Fixed locally in fides (status=0; output=$(...) || status=$?). The scaffold in kemiller2002/conditor should carry the same fix so new repositories do not inherit the masking.

items.title: EchelonFoundry.Fides.Arca bridge package: Fides.Client token provider to Arca.TokenProvider
items.description: Unblocked: conditor#59 (merged 2026-10-08) installs GitHub-release-asset NuGet libraries into a consumer's pinned local feed, and echelon-registry records arca 0.1.0. Build a package referencing EchelonFoundry.Arca.Core 0.1.0 by exact version (installed through Conditor, never a public feed) and Fides.Client, exposing toArca, with contract tests against Arca's real types (DF-FIDES-2026-0008).

items.title: Fides client: two threads could both start a refresh, and refresh tokens are single use (single-flight race)
items.description: Found by the post-completion test run for WI-0010: 'concurrent token requests share one refresh' fails 8/8 in isolation. The in-flight refresh was claimed with an unsynchronised check-then-set, so two thread-pool callers could both refresh; the second refresh would then be refused and the session wrongly revoked. Fix: claim the refresh under a lock, run it outside the lock, complete a shared TaskCompletionSource for every waiter.

items.title: Record Fides 0.1.0 in echelon-registry: release record, fides system entry, optional project binding
items.description: After the v0.1.0 release publishes: verify every asset's sha256 and attestation, add releases/fides/0.1.0.release.json and the fides system to registry/systems-v2.json, and offer fides as an optional project binding the way arca 0.1.0 was recorded (echelon-registry#45), regenerating channels with the registry's tools (DF-FIDES-2026-0006).

items.title: Conditor: the fsharp-nuget-library scaffold's *.nupkg ignore rule hides the vendor/nuget release-asset feed
items.description: Found on fides WI-0016: after conditor upgrade --current opted in to arca, vendor/nuget/*.nupkg were git-ignored by the scaffold's conditor:build-outputs region, so a commit would silently drop the feed and CI restore would fail. Fides adds !vendor/nuget/*.nupkg after the region. The scaffold region (or the feed installer) in kemiller2002/conditor should carry the exception; that fix belongs to Conditor's owner (the Arca agent for distribution).

items.title: Release Fides 0.2.0: the Aegis binding and the Arca bridge
items.description: Bump to 0.2.0 so the release workflow publishes the four packages and the Lambda package as attested GitHub release assets, verified after upload (DF-FIDES-2026-0006). The registry record is a separate item.

items.title: Record Fides 0.2.0 in echelon-registry and move echelon-current so fides resolves to 0.2.0
items.description: After v0.2.0 publishes: verify every asset's sha256 and attestation, add releases/fides/0.2.0.release.json to the catalog snapshot, regenerate the channels with the registry's tools, run its conformance checks, and prove Conditor installs fides@0.2.0 into a consumer.

items.title: Fides requirements expansion and security architecture review: complete, testable, traceable baseline (identity, authorization, data-layer, multi-organization, UX, operations, reliability), decision records, threat model, traceability matrix and Dokimos verification plan

Owner decisions on authorization, organizations, stateless limits, GitHub storage tenancy, service identities and token retention (DF-FIDES-2026-0010..0015); unblocks FID-AUZ-003..007, FID-AUZ-011, FID-ORG-001..007, FID-SVC-001..004, FID-SES-008, FID-SES-010, FID-DATA-003..004, FID-REL-001..002, FID-UX-011

Client correctness: one clock for expiry, 401 triggers refresh before revoked, outage keeps session state, boundary and restore tests (FID-REL-006..007, FID-REL-010, FID-SES-005, FID-SES-009, FID-IDN-004, FID-IDN-009)

Application-bound exchange: provider client per application or isolation domain, refresh and revoke bound to the issuing application, user-token-only repository checks, required-repository re-check on refresh (FID-DATA-006, FID-AUZ-009, FID-DATA-008, FID-AUZ-008)

Live-provider contract suite against a test GitHub App: lifetimes, rotation, single-use codes, PKCE, revocation of refresh grant, external revocation; then sign-out grant fix (FID-TEST-010..013, FID-SES-004, FID-SES-006)
Adversarial verification suite: cross-tenant, privilege escalation, fuzzed callbacks and bodies, unauthorized data access through Arca (FID-TEST-006..009)
Identity model: provider-qualified principal, authentication time, account-recovery guidance; deferred linking and MFA (FID-IDN-003, FID-IDN-006..008, FID-IDN-010)
Session lifecycle: maximum lifetime, idle timeout, cross-tab refresh lock, sign-out everywhere (FID-SES-001..003, FID-SES-010)

Operational security: correlation ids, principal in audit, alarms, access-log pin, per-source limits, supply-chain gate and SBOM, attestation refusal evidence, incident runbooks, deployment smoke test, secret rotation rehearsal (FID-OPS-002..004, FID-OPS-006..007, FID-OPS-009..014)

Fides UI on Forma and Limen: Limen integration, brand manifest, logo and landing, sign-in and callback screens, branded loading, error and expiry screens, WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard and screen reader, failure-class mapping, framing and CSP guidance (FID-UX-001..015)

Authorization ownership and data authority: ownership document review, enforcement-point inventory per application, App least-privilege check, Arca data authority (FID-AUZ-001..002, FID-AUZ-010, FID-DATA-002, FID-DATA-007)
Reliability contracts: documented timeout and retry contract, latency and availability targets after owner approval (FID-REL-001..002, FID-REL-009)

Adopt Dokimos requirement verification and a Praxis requirement catalogue: upgrade the Dokimos pin from 0.2.0, compile a verification manifest for FID-UX requirements (FID-TEST-014); threat-model review cadence (FID-OPS-011)
(Deferred) Relational data path through Strata grants and row-level policies, only if a relational store is approved (FID-DATA-005)

Authorization per accepted DF-FIDES-2026-0010 and 0013: applications adopt the default-deny decision vocabulary, classify permissions as repository-enforced, server-enforced or advisory, store roles in administrators-only repositories, prevent self-elevation, bound revocation (FID-AUZ-003..007, FID-AUZ-011)

Tenant model per accepted DF-FIDES-2026-0011: organization key, derived membership, organization switching, tenant context from trusted configuration only, one repository set per tenant (FID-ORG-001..003, FID-ORG-007, FID-DATA-003..004)
(Deferred by DF-FIDES-2026-0011) organization administration, delegation and invitations until a consumer needs more than one organization (FID-ORG-004..006)
Service identity contract per accepted DF-FIDES-2026-0014: principal kinds, installation tokens minted in the service runtime, least-privilege token requests, service audit (FID-SVC-001..004)
Token retention per accepted DF-FIDES-2026-0015: client guide risk statement and no persistence by default now; design the sealed HttpOnly refresh cookie as a versioned protocol change (FID-SES-008)

Operator deployment script for the AWS exchange: one command to set up an environment (certificate, Route 53 records, secret, package, stack, checks) and to update it to a release, prefilled for echelonfoundry.com (FID-HOST-003, FID-OPS-013)
